Content:
[MATH: i|j|k; a_{1}|a_{2}|a_{3}; b_{1}|b_{2}|b_{3}]

Example Prompt:

Explanation:
Using the determinant formula, we get

[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; 3|− 4|1; − 7|0|2|; =|− 4|1; 0|2|i −|3|1; − 7|2|j +|3|− 4; − 7|0|k; = ((− 4) ⋅ 2 − 1 ⋅ 0)i − (3 ⋅ 2 − 1 ⋅ (− 7))j + (3 ⋅ 0 − (− 4) ⋅ (− 7))k; = − 8i − 13j − 28k; = ⟨ − 8, − 13, − 28⟩.]

EXPLANATION

Using the determinant formula, we get

[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; 3|1|2x; 0|1|x|; =|1|2x; 1|x|i −|3|2x; 0|x|j +|3|1; 0|1|k; = − xi − 3xj + 3k; = ⟨ − x, − 3x, 3⟩.]

Now, computing the magnitude, we get

[MATH: |a × b||= sqrt((− x)^{2} + (− 3x)^{2} + 3^{2}); = sqrt(10x^{2} + 9).]

Lastly, we solve for [MATH: x] the following equation:

[MATH: |a × b|= sqrt(19); sqrt(10x^{2} + 9) = sqrt(19); 10x^{2} + 9 = 19; 10x^{2} = 10; x^{2} = 1]

Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x= \pm 1.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
We have been using the following formula to compute the cross product of two vectors:

Content:
[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; a_{1}|a_{2}|a_{3}; b_{1}|b_{2}|b_{3}|; =|a_{2}|a_{3}; b_{2}|b_{3}|i −|a_{1}|a_{3}; b_{1}|b_{3}|j +|a_{1}|a_{2}; b_{1}|b_{2}|k; = (a_{2}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{2})i − (a_{1}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{1})j + (a_{1}b_{2} − a_{2}b_{1})k]

Content:
But where does this formula come from? Let's find out.

Content:
Suppose we want to find the cross product [MATH: \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}] for [MATH: \mathbf{a}=a_1\mathbf{i}+a_2\mathbf{j}+a_3\mathbf{k}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}=b_1\mathbf{i}+b_2\mathbf{j}+b_3\mathbf{k}.] Using properties of the cross product, we obtain

Content:
[MATH: a × b|= (a_{1}i + a_{2}j + a_{3}k) × (b_{1}i + b_{2}j + b_{3}k); = (a_{1} ⋅ b_{1})i × i + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{2})i × j + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{3})i × k; + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{1})j × i + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{2})j × j + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{3})j × k; + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{1})k × i + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{2})k × j + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{3})k × k.]

Content:
Since the cross product of two parallel (collinear) vectors is equal to [MATH: \mathbf 0,] we have

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{i} = \mathbf{j}\times\mathbf{j} = \mathbf{k}\times\mathbf{k} = \mathbf 0.]

Content:
Also, using the definition of the cross product we obtain

Content:
[MATH: i × j = k,|j × i = − k,; j × k = i,|k × j = − i,; k × i = j,|i × k = − j.]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: a × b|= (a_{1} ⋅ b_{1})i × i_(⏟)_(= 0) + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{2})i × j_(⏟)_(= k) + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{3})i × k_(⏟)_(= − j); + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{1})j × i_(⏟)_(= − k) + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{2})j × j_(⏟)_(= 0) + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{3})j × k_(⏟)_(= i); + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{1})k × i_(⏟)_(= j) + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{2})k × j_(⏟)_(= − i) + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{3})k × k_(⏟)_(= 0); = (a_{2}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{2})i − (a_{1}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{1})j + (a_{1}b_{2} − a_{2}b_{1})k.]

Content:
The expression above is equal to the formula given for the cross product of two general vectors using the determinant.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose we have two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b},] given by

Content:
[MATH: a|= a_{1}i + a_{2}j + a_{3}k; b|= b_{1}i + b_{2}j + b_{3}k.]

Content:
The cross product [MATH: \mathbf{a}\times\mathbf b] can be calculated using the following determinant:

Content:
[MATH: i|j|k; a_{1}|a_{2}|a_{3}; b_{1}|b_{2}|b_{3}]

Content:
For instance, suppose that we have the two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a} = \langle 2,-1,5 \rangle], [MATH: \mathbf{b} = \langle -1,4,2 \rangle]. We can find the cross product of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; 2|− 1|5; − 1|4|2|; =|− 1|5; 4|2|i −|2|5; − 1|2|j +|2|− 1; − 1|4|k; = ((− 1) ⋅ 2 − 5 ⋅ 4)i − (2 ⋅ 2 − 5 ⋅ (− 1))j + (2 ⋅ 4 − (− 1) ⋅ (− 1))k; = − 22i − 9j + 7k; = ⟨ − 22, − 9, 7⟩]

Item 2 — Example: Calculating the Cross Product Using Determinants

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the determinant formula, we get

[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; 3|− 4|1; − 7|0|2|; =|− 4|1; 0|2|i −|3|1; − 7|2|j +|3|− 4; − 7|0|k; = ((− 4) ⋅ 2 − 1 ⋅ 0)i − (3 ⋅ 2 − 1 ⋅ (− 7))j + (3 ⋅ 0 − (− 4) ⋅ (− 7))k; = − 8i − 13j − 28k; = ⟨ − 8, − 13, − 28⟩.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Proof of the Formula for the Cross Product Using the Determinant

Content:
We have been using the following formula to compute the cross product of two vectors:

Content:
[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; a_{1}|a_{2}|a_{3}; b_{1}|b_{2}|b_{3}|; =|a_{2}|a_{3}; b_{2}|b_{3}|i −|a_{1}|a_{3}; b_{1}|b_{3}|j +|a_{1}|a_{2}; b_{1}|b_{2}|k; = (a_{2}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{2})i − (a_{1}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{1})j + (a_{1}b_{2} − a_{2}b_{1})k]

Content:
But where does this formula come from? Let's find out.

Content:
Suppose we want to find the cross product [MATH: \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}] for [MATH: \mathbf{a}=a_1\mathbf{i}+a_2\mathbf{j}+a_3\mathbf{k}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}=b_1\mathbf{i}+b_2\mathbf{j}+b_3\mathbf{k}.] Using properties of the cross product, we obtain

Content:
[MATH: a × b|= (a_{1}i + a_{2}j + a_{3}k) × (b_{1}i + b_{2}j + b_{3}k); = (a_{1} ⋅ b_{1})i × i + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{2})i × j + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{3})i × k; + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{1})j × i + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{2})j × j + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{3})j × k; + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{1})k × i + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{2})k × j + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{3})k × k.]

Content:
Since the cross product of two parallel (collinear) vectors is equal to [MATH: \mathbf 0,] we have

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{i} = \mathbf{j}\times\mathbf{j} = \mathbf{k}\times\mathbf{k} = \mathbf 0.]

Content:
Also, using the definition of the cross product we obtain

Content:
[MATH: i × j = k,|j × i = − k,; j × k = i,|k × j = − i,; k × i = j,|i × k = − j.]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: a × b|= (a_{1} ⋅ b_{1})i × i_(⏟)_(= 0) + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{2})i × j_(⏟)_(= k) + (a_{1} ⋅ b_{3})i × k_(⏟)_(= − j); + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{1})j × i_(⏟)_(= − k) + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{2})j × j_(⏟)_(= 0) + (a_{2} ⋅ b_{3})j × k_(⏟)_(= i); + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{1})k × i_(⏟)_(= j) + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{2})k × j_(⏟)_(= − i) + (a_{3} ⋅ b_{3})k × k_(⏟)_(= 0); = (a_{2}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{2})i − (a_{1}b_{3} − a_{3}b_{1})j + (a_{1}b_{2} − a_{2}b_{1})k.]

Content:
The expression above is equal to the formula given for the cross product of two general vectors using the determinant.
